boards.title: Only Happens Here: 10 Traditions That Make No Sense Anywhere Else
boards.description: Ten documented CU Boulder traditions, ceremonies and recurring community events.

cards.title: Watch Ralphie’s iconic run
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder home football games
cards.notes: At a home game, arrive before kickoff to see CU Boulder’s live buffalo mascot run across the field with student Ralphie Runners.
cards.short_summary: A live-buffalo kickoff ritual dating to 1967.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder’s Alumni Association says Ralphie’s run began in 1967 and occurs at the start of every home football game and near the end of halftime.
cards.source_title: Top 10 CU Boulder traditions that bring Buffs together
cards.access_notes: See the athletics schedule and game-entry requirements before attending.

cards.title: Join the Conference on World Affairs
cards.subtitle: Annual CU Boulder speaker conference
cards.notes: Browse the annual program and choose a session that interests you; students receive priority seating for this campus-wide conversation series.
cards.short_summary: An annual week of public conversations with hundreds of sessions.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder describes the Conference on World Affairs as an annual event with more than 200 sessions over several days; it is free and open to the public.
cards.source_title: Top 10 CU Boulder traditions that bring Buffs together
cards.access_notes: Check the current program for session locations and seating details.

cards.title: Mark graduation at Grad Bash
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder Alumni Association graduation event
cards.notes: If you are graduating, check the Alumni Association’s Grad Bash details and join the class celebration before commencement season concludes.
cards.short_summary: A graduation-season gathering for CU Boulder’s graduating class.
cards.evidence_claim: The Herd identifies Grad Bash as a CU Boulder Alumni Association graduation celebration and states that the event is free and includes a graduation gift.
cards.access_notes: For graduating students; confirm current event details and registration requirements.

cards.title: Return for CU Boulder Homecoming
cards.subtitle: Annual fall Buffs gathering
cards.notes: Follow the current Homecoming itinerary for campus events and reunions, then take in the evolving rituals that have connected Buffs since 1914.
cards.short_summary: CU Boulder’s alumni-and-student homecoming tradition began in 1914.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder records its first official Homecoming celebration on Nov. 7, 1914 and says alumni continue to return to celebrate the tradition.
cards.access_notes: Event dates and registration vary each year; use the current Homecoming itinerary.

cards.title: See the BolderBoulder finish at Folsom Field
cards.subtitle: Memorial Day 10K in Boulder
cards.notes: If participating or spectating, consult the race’s current information and plan around its distinctive finish inside Folsom Field.
cards.short_summary: Boulder’s Memorial Day 10K culminates in CU Boulder’s stadium.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder’s Alumni Association calls the BolderBoulder a Colorado Memorial Day tradition and notes its finish inside Folsom Field.
cards.source_title: Top 10 CU Boulder traditions that bring Buffs together
cards.access_notes: Race entry, route access and spectator guidance are set by the event organizer.

cards.title: Attend the Colorado Shakespeare Festival
cards.subtitle: Annual CU Boulder summer theater tradition
cards.notes: Review the current festival season and select a performance at the Mary Rippon Outdoor Theatre or Roe Green Theatre.
cards.short_summary: A CU Boulder summer festival presenting outdoor and indoor theater.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder says the Colorado Shakespeare Festival has been held annually since 1958, with productions at the Mary Rippon Outdoor Theatre and Roe Green Theatre.
cards.source_title: Top 10 CU Boulder traditions that bring Buffs together
cards.access_notes: Performance dates, tickets and venue guidance vary by season.

cards.title: Listen for the Macky carillon
cards.subtitle: Macky Auditorium, CU Boulder
cards.notes: Pause near Macky Auditorium at the top of an hour to hear the keyboard-played carillon bells carry across campus.
cards.short_summary: Macky’s carillon continues CU Boulder’s bell tradition.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder’s Senior Class Council says Macky Auditorium’s carillon bells can be heard across campus at the top of the hour.
cards.access_notes: Listen from public campus areas; sound may vary with weather and campus activity.

cards.entity_name: CU Boulder Alma Mater at Commencement
cards.title: Sing CU Boulder’s alma mater
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder commencement ceremony
cards.notes: At commencement, join classmates, professors and guests in singing the alma mater as part of the university’s graduation ceremony.
cards.short_summary: A shared song that closes the student chapter into alumni life.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder’s commencement office identifies singing the CU Boulder alma mater with classmates, professors and guests as a commencement tradition.
cards.access_notes: This tradition occurs as part of commencement; attendance follows ceremony requirements.

cards.title: Hear the Norlin Charge
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder commencement ritual
cards.notes: Listen for the Norlin Charge during commencement and note its connection to President George Norlin’s 1935 address.
cards.short_summary: A 1935 presidential charge preserved in CU Boulder graduation ritual.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder says the Norlin Charge has inspired University of Colorado graduates since President George Norlin delivered it in 1935.
cards.access_notes: Presented during commencement; consult the current ceremony program for details.

cards.title: Practice the student-created Colorado Creed
cards.subtitle: CU Boulder community responsibility code
cards.notes: Read the Colorado Creed before campus events and use its honor, respect and community-minded commitments to guide participation.
cards.short_summary: A CU Boulder values tradition created by students in 2003.
cards.evidence_claim: CU Boulder says the Colorado Creed is a social responsibility code developed by students in 2003 and describes the commitments it asks Buffs to uphold.
cards.source_title: What It Means to Be a Buff
cards.access_notes: Available to all members of the CU Boulder community; no event admission is involved.
